pass_means: SELF-CHECK = internal consistency only: identities, convergence and agreement with our own closed forms.  It says NOTHING about agreement with the publication; that is the 'verdict' column of the summary table in docs/validation/published_benchmarks.md, and several rows there disagree while the self-check passes.
note: Axisymmetric m = 0 full wave (docs/validation/fullwave.md).  The readout is driven uniformly around the axis: exact while the readout loop's circumference is small compared with the wavelength, and the uniform-feed limit otherwise.  DMRadio-m^3's coax 'funnels to a narrow neck coupled to the matching circuit above', i.e. an on-axis (axisymmetric) feed, so the model is appropriate; DMRadio-Core is read out through a 30-degree sector of its slit, so for Core these are the uniform-feed limit only.

m3_self_resonances.published_prediction: c/(4 h_coax), the pole of Z_p = i Z_c tan(omega h/c) (M3_EM Eq. 2, L350-375), for an ideal line with no end effect
m3_self_resonances.note: Our m = 0 poles sit 9-25 % below c/(4 h_coax), and the deficit grows as the coax gets shorter.  A single open-end length extension dl (independent of h, set by the gap width) absorbs all of it: that is the standard fringing correction the ideal lossless-line formula omits.  Separately, the TE111 mode at ~100 MHz is an m = 1 mode that an axisymmetric solver cannot see; M3_EM L509-516 puts it at 125-185 MHz for coaxes 1-5, and it is the mode their single-mode requirement is about.

core_scan_time_beyond_mqs.eta_A: published dc-SQUID optimum, frequency by frequency
core_scan_time_beyond_mqs.note: Time to cover 70-140 MHz at DFSZ, integrating the local scan rate with the local F.  'MQS' uses the constant omega -> 0 F; the full-wave columns use F(omega) from the sweep, with L(omega) = -Im Z/omega and with DMRadio's Foster L_eff.  The gap between them is how much of DMRadio-Core's reach comes from operating near the pickup's self-resonance, which the MQS numbers cannot see.

pass_scope: the six coax self-resonances against the published c/(4 h) with a single fitted open-end extension (a genuine agreement with an independent published model), plus sweep sanity.  It does NOT test any scan time.
headline: m3: the six published coaxes resonate up to 24 % below c/(4 h), all absorbed by one open-end extension dl = 16 cm = 0.55 x the gap width (residual 2.8 %); MQS good to 7.8 MHz (5 %) for the tallest; Core pickups resonate at 155, 129 MHz
